title: The Sky Speaks, God's Teaching Guides
overview: This psalm praises God first for the sky, which silently speaks of him, then for his teaching, and ends with a humble prayer to be cleared of wrongdoing.

parts.label: The silent voice of the sky (vv. 1-4a)
parts.note: The poet pictures the sky as constantly announcing that God made it, even though it uses no words, so its message reaches every people on earth. Christians later read verse 4 as a picture of the message about Jesus spreading worldwide, as Paul does in Romans 10:18.

parts.label: The sun's daily run (vv. 4b-6)
parts.note: The sun is pictured as a glowing bridegroom and an eager runner, crossing the sky each day and warming everything beneath it. Neighboring peoples often worshiped the sun as a god, but here it is simply something God made and gave a tent to live in.

parts.label: God's teaching praised (vv. 7-9)
parts.note: The poem turns from the sky to the LORD's law, a word that means instruction or guidance, not only rules, and gives it six names, each paired with a good effect such as renewing a person or making inexperienced people wise. The fear of the LORD here means deep respect for God, which the poet praises as spotless and lasting forever.

parts.label: Worth more than gold (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: The poet says this teaching is more valuable than the finest gold and sweeter than honey straight from the comb, the richest sweetness people then knew. It warns of danger, and living by it brings real good.

parts.label: A prayer about hidden faults (vv. 12-13)
parts.note: Seeing God's standards makes the poet aware of wrongs they cannot even spot in themselves, so they ask to be cleared of them. They also ask to be held back from deliberate, arrogant wrongdoing before it takes control of their life.

parts.label: Closing prayer (v. 14)
parts.note: The poet hopes everything they have said and thought will please God. Calling God a Rock means a solid, safe refuge, and a redeemer was the close relative who bought back family land or freed a relative sold into slavery.

disagreement: Christians genuinely differ on how much the natural world by itself can tell people about God, with some seeing it as a real path to knowing him and others holding that it only points the way and needs God's spoken word to be understood.
think: When you look at a night sky or a sunrise, does it seem to say anything to you, and if so, what?
